subject: SLA: monthly credit scaling & latency grace for batched workloads
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine@cumulusdata.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cumulusdata.com
Date: 2027-04-01T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Request: SLA exceptions for scheduled batch inference

Dylan —

Thanks for the demo last week. We ran the performance tests against our production batch windows and want to surface an important constraint on our side: our batsched jobs are large (multi-hour, low QPS) and cannot be rehoused easily. Practically that means we need an SLA carveout for scheduled batched inference where the standard 99.95% uptime target is unrealistic.

Request summary:
- Uptime target for scheduled batched nodes: 99.5% (monthly)
- Latency: allow a tail-latency grace (95th within SLO, 99th allowed exceptions during peak daily ingress)
- Monthly credit ask: tiered credits that escalate starting at 30 minutes of cumulative downtime

Attached is a short redline (Cumulus_SLA_Request.pdf) that shows our suggested credit bands and a short rationale. Can Redwood share a counter that shows how credits would map to a typical spend profile? We have an internal procurement cutoff for April 20.

Thanks — Elaine
Elaine Park
Head of Platform Engineering, Cumulus Data
attachment: Cumulus_SLA_Request.pdf (pdf)

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@cumulusdata.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-02T11:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA exceptions for scheduled batch inference

Elaine — thanks for the clear ask and for the data during the test window. We appreciate the context; batch workloads do have different availability trade-offs.

High-level counterproposal (summary):
- Keep hosted interactive endpoints at 99.95%.
- For scheduled batched inference (customer-managed batch pools / reserved nodes): set a separate SLA at 99.5% monthly as you requested, but with stricter measurement and an agreed maintenance window cadence.
- Monthly credit structure (proposed):
  * 30–120 minutes downtime: credit = 5% of monthly invoice for the impacted RIs
  * 121–240 minutes: credit = 15%
  * 241–480 minutes: credit = 35%
  * >480 minutes: credit = 60% (capped at 100% for extreme outage investigations)
- Cap: maximum credit per month for a single account = 50% of monthly committed spend (we can discuss exceptions).
- Latency: allow an appendix that exempts 99th percentile latency during platform-wide ingress surges or planned tuning windows; 95th must still meet the agreed SLO.

We'll attach an editable tier table and a small latency appendix for your team to review. Ben and Aditya — can you check that the credit caps above sit with finance/legal and that we have a clean definition for "downtime" vs degraded tail-latency?

Next steps:
1) We will send the redline (attached) and a spreadsheet with example calculations mapped to typical monthly spends.
2) If that looks acceptable, we can prepare an amendment for signature (DocuSign) by April 12 to make procurement timelines.

Thanks — appreciate the quick turn.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attachment: Redwood_SLA_TieredCreditTable.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-03T08:32:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: draft credit bands and measurement notes for Cumulus

Dylan — quick thoughts from finance/legal POV. High level fine, but please note:
- Cap guidance: Finance prefers a hard cap of 50% monthly for committed contracts; procurement will push for lower, but we should not go above 60% in negotiation.
- Measurement: define "downtime" precisely — recommend: consecutive unavailability for an endpoint grouped into incidents; cumulative minutes is sum of incident durations where successful retries fail for >5 minutes. Exclude scheduled maintenance with 72-hour notice.
- Latency carveout: engineering must provide a deterministic definition of burst windows (e.g., >2x baseline QPS for >10 minutes) to avoid open-ended exemptions.
- Example calc: for a $120k monthly commit, 121–240 minutes => 15% credit = $18k applied to next invoice. Need to make sure we can apply credits vs direct refunds per accounting rules.

Laura — can Legal prepare a short amendment that uses these bands and a defined measurement appendix (Aditya may help with metrics)?

Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Commercial Finance

From: Markus Engel <markus.engel@cumulusdata.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Elaine Park <elaine@cumulusdata.com>, procurement@cumulusdata.com
Date: 2027-04-05T14:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA exceptions for scheduled batch inference

Dylan — thanks for the quick counter. A few points from procurement:
- The cap at 50% is a non-starter for us; we will propose a 25% absolute cap in the amendment.
- Request: provide a worked example for our typical 350k/mo committed spend and one for a 30k/mo pilot. Include both credit impact and timeline to apply credits.
- For latency carveouts, we need a concrete definition of the burst window and a monitoring hook we can call (an API to get incident status) so our SREs can correlate.

I attached our standard PO template and the procurement team's redline with the 25% cap. If Redwood can give the worked examples and an updated amendment reflecting the measurement definitions, we'll escalate internally to exec review.

Markus
Markus Engel
VP, Procurement — Cumulus Data
attachment: Cumulus_PO_Template.pdf (pdf)
attachment: Cumulus_Procurement_Redline.docx (docx)

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Markus Engel <markus.engel@cumulusdata.com>, Elaine Park <elaine@cumulusdata.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-07T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA exceptions for scheduled batch inference — next steps

Markus / Elaine — thanks. Quick summary / commitments from Redwood: 

1) We will produce two worked examples by EOD 2027-04-08: one for $350k/mo committed spend and one for a $30k pilot. Spreadsheet attached (Redwood_SLA_TieredCreditTable.xlsx).
2) Legal will draft an amendment with two alternative cap lines (25% requested by Cumulus vs Redwood's 50% cap). Please indicate which cap you prefer; we can include a short escalation path for exec approval if the higher cap is needed.
3) Engineering (Aditya) will draft a short Latency SLO Appendix that:
   - defines burst window (2x baseline QPS for >10 minutes)
   - provides an incident API endpoint and incident ID format for cross-correlation
Attachment: Latency_SLO_Appendix.pdf included for review.
4) Target: sign amendment via DocuSign by 2027-04-12 to hit procurement cutoffs. HubSpot deal CUM-2027-7893 updated with the amendment link.

Please let me know if the timeline is infeasible. If Cumulus wants the 25% cap, flag it and we'll include the ask in the amendment so execs can review quickly.

Best — Dylan
attachment: Latency_SLO_Appendix.pdf (pdf), Redwood_SLA_TieredCreditTable.xlsx (xlsx)
